intro: Gmail for legal secretaries on Mac is best managed through a browser or a dedicated web app, as Google does not offer a native desktop client. You can optimize your workflow by enabling keyboard shortcuts and using tools like Lazur to manage your inbox by voice.
tldr: There is no official Gmail app for Mac, so use a browser or create a web app.
Enable keyboard shortcuts in Settings to save time on common tasks.
Use Lazur to dictate complex emails or ask for guidance on Gmail features.
Maintain strict file organization using labels and filters to handle high email volumes.
Keep track of daily sending limits to avoid account blocks during busy periods.

blocks.text: Setting up Gmail for legal secretaries on Mac

Since you do not have a native app, create a web app. Open Gmail in Safari. Go to File > Add to Dock. This creates a dedicated icon in your Dock. It acts like an app. You get notifications and can switch to it with ⌘ + Tab. This keeps your legal correspondence separate from browser tabs. It helps you focus on your inbox.
Essential keyboard shortcuts for legal work

Shortcuts turn hours of clicking into seconds of work. First, go to Settings > General > Keyboard shortcuts. Turn them on. Now, use c to compose. Use / to search. Use e to archive. Press ? to see all shortcuts. This is the fastest way to move through case files and client requests.

items: j/k: Move down or up through emails

blocks.text: Lazur helps you stay in your flow. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen. If you forget where the filter settings are, ask Lazur. It circles the button for you. If you need to dictate a long, formal email, hold fn and speak. Lazur types it at your cursor. It saves you from repetitive typing.

Legal files require precision. Use labels for every case. Create a label for each client or matter. Go to Settings > Labels to manage them. Use filters to route emails automatically. If an email contains a specific case number, have it move to that label. This keeps your inbox clean. You can find documents faster when they are sorted correctly.

items: Do not send attachments over 25MB. Use Google Drive links instead.
Check your recipients carefully. The 2,000 limit for Workspace includes To, Cc, and Bcc.
Enable Undo Send in Settings. Set it to 30 seconds. It saves you from sending incomplete drafts.
Use labels instead of folders. Emails can have multiple labels, which is better for complex cases.

blocks.text: Legal secretaries often handle large PDFs. Gmail handles files well, but keep an eye on size. If you hit the limit, upload the file to Google Drive. Then, insert the link into your email. This ensures your message sends without errors. Use the search bar to find old attachments. Type has:attachment to narrow down your results.

Security is paramount. Use two-factor authentication on your Google account. If your firm uses shared mailboxes, use the delegation feature. Go to Settings > Accounts and Import > Grant access to your account. This allows you to manage the mailbox without sharing your password. Google only supports clients that use OAuth. Avoid any app that asks for your direct password.

faq.question: Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google does not provide a native Gmail desktop app. You should use a web browser or create a web app using Safari or Chrome.

faq.question: How do I turn on keyboard shortcuts?
faq.answer: Go to Gmail Settings, click See all settings, stay in the General tab, scroll to Keyboard shortcuts, and select Keyboard shortcuts on.

faq.question: What is the daily email limit?
faq.answer: For personal accounts, the limit is 500 recipients. For Google Workspace accounts, the limit is 2,000 recipients per day.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. It points at items, answers questions, and dictates text so you can work faster.
